name: Ransomware with data extortion
summary: An attacker gains a foothold, steals credentials, moves laterally, exfiltrates data and then encrypts systems, threatening to publish the stolen data unless a ransom is paid ("double extortion").

attack_path.description: Phishing email with a malicious attachment, or login to an exposed remote access service with stolen credentials.
Scripts run on the first host and credentials are dumped from memory.
The attacker maps accounts and servers and moves between hosts over RDP.
Sensitive data is uploaded to attacker-controlled cloud storage before encryption.
Security tools are disabled, backups and shadow copies are deleted, services are stopped and files are encrypted.

key_decisions: When to declare an incident and who has the authority to do so
Whether to isolate systems or the whole network, accepting business downtime
Whether to engage law enforcement, outside counsel and a forensics firm
Whether paying the ransom is legally permitted and acceptable to leadership
Which systems to restore first, and how to confirm backups are clean
